title: Resolve _xlfn.-prefixed function names in a loaded formula to the catalogue function
description:
## Outcome
A formula loaded from a file that spells a function with Excel's file prefix (_xlfn.IFNA, _xlfn.MAXIFS, _xlfn._xlws.FILTER) compiles to the same catalogue function as its plain name, so calc_fml, calc_engine and calc_host compute it; the document keeps the file text unchanged, so a save writes the prefix back as loaded.

## Context
The first cargo xtask compare run (dc-kt3l, 2026-10-21): Default-tariff-cap-level spells IFNA as _xlfn.IFNA in 49 formulas whose results 62,786 other formula cells read, and calc_fml's compile refuses _xlfn.IFNA as UnknownFunction because it looks the spelling up as written (crates/calc-fml/src/eval/compile.rs). Every function Excel added after 2007 is stored with the prefix (MAXIFS, MINIFS, IFNA, XLOOKUP, CONCAT, FILTER), so loaded workbooks meet the same refusal. dc-552j owns the save half (adding prefixes to authored text from catalogue metadata) and converting UI text to file form; this bead takes only name resolution of the file form.

## Do
- In calc_fml's compile, resolve a call whose name carries the _xlfn. prefix, optionally followed by _xlws., by the name after the prefixes; keep the spelling as written for diagnostics; refuse as now when the plain name is not catalogued. Whether an unprefixed spelling of a prefixed function, or a prefixed spelling of a function Excel never prefixes, is accepted follows what Excel does when it loads such a file (measure it, or refuse with a typed refusal naming dc-552j).
- A case that compiles and evaluates =_xlfn.IFNA(...), =_xlfn.MAXIFS(...) (or catalogued functions that carry the prefix) through calc_fml::evaluate, and opens a generator-built package holding them through calc_host, with the cells calculated.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform wasm --require-all
```
_xlfn.-prefixed calls of catalogued functions compute through calc_fml::evaluate and through calc_host on a loaded package; an unknown prefixed name is still refused as UnknownFunction with its spelling.

## Out of scope
Adding prefixes on save, error constants on save, UI text conversion (dc-552j).

title: Refuse a CellReader that repeats or reorders cells in every aggregate kernel
description:
## Outcome
Every aggregate kernel refuses a CellReader that breaks its contract (a cell outside the area, cells out of row-major order, a cell visited twice) instead of counting a repeated cell twice.

## Context
cfunc-m3.4 (2026-10-20, round-2 judge): the kernels enforce the CellReader contract unevenly (crates/calc-func/src/catalogue/aggregate.rs, read_reference and SUMPRODUCT's factor). Every kernel refuses an outside visit, only SUMPRODUCT refuses out-of-order visits, and COUNTBLANK catches duplicates only beyond the area's size, so SUM, COUNT and AVERAGE would add a repeated cell twice. Robustness only: calc-fml's reader (ReaderCells) keeps the contract. The cfunc_m3_4 acceptance case already drives readers that breach it (Breach::Outside, Reversed, Twice). CalcFunc files only.

## Do
Check order and repeats once, in read_reference, so every kernel gets the same refusal (ReferenceUnreadable); extend the breach rows to every kernel.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id cfunc-m3.4 --platform windows --require-all
```
A reader that visits a held cell twice or out of order ends every aggregate kernel in ReferenceUnreadable.

## Out of scope
The reader implementations themselves (calc-fml, calc-engine).

title: Report each executed call's arguments and result, so a comparison names the kernel call instead of inferring it
description:
## Outcome
calc_fml's evaluation reports, for each executed catalogue call, its argument values and its result, so a comparison can name the call whose result a formula returned and the arguments it was given, instead of inferring them.

## Context
dc-kt3l (cargo xtask compare, 2026-10-21) classes a calculated cell that differs from Excel and reads no other differing cell as kernel-value or kernel-bits, keyed by the last call compile did not insert. ExecutedCall (crates/calc-fml/src/eval/mod.rs) exposes only target() and synthetic(), so both the class and the key are inferred, and triage.json's attribution says so. The Ofgem comparison (dc-3t1b) does not wait on this: its kernel keys are filed as inferred. A kernel bead filed from a mismatch needs the arguments to reproduce it.

## Do
- ExecutedCall (or the observer's report) carries each call's argument values as the kernel was given them and its result, additively, at no cost when no observer asks.
- cargo xtask compare keys a kernel difference by the call whose result the formula returned, records its arguments, and marks the attribution reported instead of inferred.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
```
A case where a formula calls two functions and the outer one's result differs: the triage names the outer call, its arguments and result as reported.

## Out of scope
Changing what the evaluator computes.

title: Measure Excel formula-text rules with one owner capture
description:
## Outcome
One owner capture measures the formula-text rules that CalcFml and CalcDoc state but have not measured, and each rule in the code matches Excel's measured behaviour or names the difference.

## Context
Found by the cfml-m1.2 and cdoc-m1.2 reviews (2026-10-20). The rules are written down as not measured in migration/ports/cfml-m1.2.json and in calc-doc's load doc. Only the owner runs Excel. One generated workbook and one `cargo xtask capture` cover them all.

## Do
Write a committed generator for one oracle workbook, plus the owner's capture of it, covering:
- Off-grid relative references, per route: A1 copy, fill, R1C1 entry and defined names. Does Excel give #REF! or wrap? (calc_fml::PlacementError::worksheet_error says #REF!.)
- The qualifier-character test: `[ ] \ /` read as an external workbook, `:` as a sheet span. Also `=B3:Sheet2!D7` and `=Sheet2!SUM(A1)`.
- Lower-case r/c in R1C1; `R[+2]C`; cell-like text outside the grid (XFE1, Sales2023) read as a name.
- Formula length: is the 8,192 limit counted in UTF-16 units or characters, does `=` count, and what does Excel do when it opens a longer formula (calc-doc FORMULA_MAX_UTF16_CODE_UNITS)?
- `_xHHHH_` in formula text: does Excel escape it when it writes, and does it decode it when it reads (calc-doc load/sheet.rs)?
Then align the code with what was measured, or state each difference in the migration record and the doc it contradicts.

## Acceptance
The capture record is committed. For each rule, a case reads the capture through calc_verdict::judge, and reports not_run until the capture exists.

## Out of scope
Sheet-name rules (dc-85qk). Function semantics (cfunc-m1.2's oracle).
notes:
From cdoc-m1.2 (2026-10-20), more rules for the same capture: what Excel writes or reads for a shared-formula member moved past the grid and for a chained range (A:B:C) in a shared master (calc-doc refuses both today, failing the whole load); an empty <v> on a constant number cell (refused as InvalidNumber today); and a boundary formula of exactly the formula-length limit plus one a unit longer, so the case can assert both sides.

From dc-4r8u (2026-10-20, eb669eb), readings to measure in the same capture: `={A1}` (refused at entry?), `=Sheet2!#REF!` (gives #REF!?), `=#REF!(A1)`, `=$B`, `=$3`, `=Sheet2!$B`, `=Sheet2!$3` (each refused?), and `=Sheet2!A1:Sheet1!B2` (read as two references or refused?). Also `R[+2]C`, which the binder accepts; the cfml-m1.2 record no longer carries that note, so this bead's context should point here rather than at the record.

title: Carry array results in CaptureRecord and compare arrays in calc-verdict
description:
## Outcome
CaptureRecord carries a formula cell's array result (its shape and each element's raw value) and calc-verdict compares arrays element by element, so a spilling formula is scored, not left as a per-cell spill failure.

## Context
dc-xb26 (2026-10-20) records a cell that spills after Excel's rebuild as a typed per-cell 'spill' failure whose message names the range, rows and columns; calc-verdict counts it not_run. The shape is text, and STAGE_SPILL is outside calc-verdict's stage vocabulary (tools/calc-verdict/src/session.rs). Plan 10.1/10.2 make array shape part of the comparison. Needed when dynamic-array functions are scored against Excel (cfunc-m3.16, cfunc-m3.17) and when the engine spills (ceng spill beads). Infrastructure files (calc-oracle-excel, calc-verdict).

## Do
- Add an array observation to CaptureRecord (a new record version if needed): rows, columns and each element's raw value as the scalar observations already are.
- The worker reads the spill range's Value2 after the rebuild and after reopen.
- calc-verdict compares an array result with an array observation element by element and by shape; a scalar against an array is a mismatch, never a pass.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m1.1 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id dc-xb26 --platform windows --require-all
```
A stand-in capture of a 3-by-2 spill is recorded as an array and judged matched against an equal array result, mismatched against a different element or shape.

## Out of scope
Legacy CSE arrays (infra-m7.4).
notes: From dc-xb26 round 2 (2026-10-20): (1) a spilling anchor is a plain not_run CellVerdict, told apart from a missing observation only through failures.by_stage["spill"]; the anchor's input dynamic-array claim is reset and the validated spill_members are dropped (platform/calc-oracle-excel/src/convert.rs), so the record holds no spill-child population (plan 10.1): carry the shape, the children and the claim. (2) calc-verdict's docs describe the old record: tools/calc-verdict/src/capture.rs FormulaCell::dynamic_array says the input ref is the cell itself (the adapter now flags a non-spilling cell whose input ref was B1:C3), session.rs's stage list lacks `spill`, and its saved/reopened doc says they hold every inventory cell (spill anchors no longer do); fix them with the record change (infra-m1.1 wasm then runs too). description:

The excel and wasm not_run branches (Excel not registered, runner or driver missing; accept.rs:417-426, 464, 1016-1019) are exercised by no test. Infrastructure files only (tools/xtask). Plan section 10.4: a wasm compile-only job is not browser validation.

title: Expose an edit's reach from open so the host can keep unreached file caches FileCached
description:
## Outcome
calc_engine lets its caller tell which formula cells a committed edit reached, from the moment a workbook opens, so CalcHost can keep an unreached file cache labelled FileCached after an edit and retire its conservative StaleCause::FileCacheUnverified.

## Context
chost-m1.1 (2026-10-20, round-2 judge): EngineState::with_file_caches leaves every formula node pending with no prerequisites filed, and calc_engine exposes no closure of a prepared or committed change. CalcHost therefore cannot tell an edit's reach before the first recalculation, and after the first committed edit that changes an input it labels every as-opened file cache Stale with cause FileCacheUnverified (crates/calc-host/src/project.rs), including cells no edit reached (Calc!B1 in chost_m1_1__recalc_failure_keeps_edit). Honesty rule 2 asks that this conservative broadening be owned by a bead naming its replacement: this one. Library: CalcEngine; then the CalcHost change that retires the cause.

## Do
- Bind formulas at EngineState::with_file_caches (file their prerequisites) so the dependency graph exists before the first recalculation.
- Expose the closure of one prepared or committed change (for example CommitReceipt::reached: the formula cells it reaches).
- Retire StaleCause::FileCacheUnverified in calc-host: a file cache an edit did not reach stays FileCached; one it reached projects Stale with cause AwaitingRecalc or RecalcFailed.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id ceng-m1.2 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id chost-m1.1 --platform windows --require-all
```
After an edit that changes an input, a file-cached formula the edit did not reach (Calc!B1 in chost_m1_1__recalc_failure_keeps_edit) projects FileCached, and every reached one projects Stale with its cause.

title: Deploy DNA Calc and DNA OneCalc to dnacalc.com, and use dna-koderbot as a test machine
description:
## Outcome
DNA Calc is served at https://dnacalc.com and DNA OneCalc at https://onecalc.dnacalc.com, from releases the owner publishes to dna-koderbot. dna-koderbot also works as a Linux test machine for the repository: it runs CI and the acceptance sweep in an isolated container, and its failures are raised as GitHub issues that the infra clone triages into beads.

## Context
Owner request (2026-10-18): plan and bead out a deployment strategy that starts deploying to dna-koderbot, and uses dna-koderbot as a work machine for testing and raising issues. The existing content of dnacalc.com may be removed and replaced. Plan from workflow wf_74ca3b42-eea; the owner's decisions are held in dc-oy6l.

Strategy:
dna-koderbot does two separate jobs.
1. **Work machine.** A self-hosted runner in an unprivileged LXD container runs Linux CI and acceptance for koderbot.yml only. Failures become GitHub issues, which the infra clone triages into beads.
2. **Site host.** dnacalc.com becomes the home page for DNA OneCalc (onecalc.dnacalc.com) and DNA Calc (calc.dnacalc.com). The owner publishes from his own clone through a forced-command receiver. Each app host gets DNS and Caddy only at that app's first approved publish.

There is no CI publish route on GitHub Free.

Architecture:
**Repository (DnaCalc/DnaCalc, master; Infrastructure except apps/*/web)**
- `.github/workflows/koderbot.yml` (K1b–K4), owner-pushed:
  - triggers: push to master, schedule `17 2 * * *`, dispatch (probe_memory, accept_ids, inject_failure);
  - concurrency group `dnacalc-koderbot-${{github.event_name}}`;
  - job koderbot-linux: `[self-hosted, linux, x64, dnacalc-ci]`, contents: read;
  - job raise-issues: ubuntu-24.04, issues: write.
- `.github/workflows/site.yml` (S2), owner-pushed: schedule plus dispatch only, contents: read, no secrets. It runs `site verify --drift` and `--hosts`.
- `deploy/koderbot/` (K1a, K4): lxd/dnacalc-ci.yaml, provision.sh, probe.sh, job-started.sh, OWNER_STEPS.md, identity.json, legacy/*.
- `deploy/host/` (R1): dnacalc-site-receive (Python 3.12+) and sshd-dnacalc-deploy.conf.
- `deploy/caddy/`: headers.caddy plus one file per host (S1, S2, O2, C2); expect.json and CUTOVER.md (S2).
- `deploy/site/home/` (S1); `deploy/site/published.json` (format S2, entries committed by the owner).
- `apps/dna-onecalc/web`, `apps/dna-calc/web` (O1, C1): index.html, main.js, optional worker.js, site.json.
- `tools/xtask`: accept-sweep and `accept --receipt-dir` (W1); `site pack|publish|rollback|status|verify|bundle|smoke` (S1, S2, S3); ci-issues (K3).

**Work machine (dna-koderbot: Ubuntu 25.10 KVM, 16 vCPU, 61 GiB RAM, no swap)**
- LXD container dnacalc-ci (ubuntu:24.04): unprivileged, no nesting.
- Limits: 8 CPU, 24 GiB memory, swap off, 8192 processes, CPU priority 2. Disk priority only if the scheduler is bfq, otherwise limits.read/limits.write.
- Disk: 140 GiB root on a 150 GiB btrfs loop pool.
- Network: lxdbr0 with NAT, and an egress ACL that rejects 169.254/16, RFC 1918 and the host's own addresses, except bridge DNS and DHCP. No host disks.
- Runner and toolchain: root-owned under /opt, read-only to user `runner`, with `--disableupdate` and the job-started hook in /etc/dnacalc-ci. One runner instance means one job and one cargo at a time.
- Snapshot `clean`, restored on a schedule.

**Site host**
- Caddy 2.6.2 imports /etc/caddy/dnacalc/*.caddy, one file per moved host. Legacy blocks stay in the Caddyfile until each host's approval. koderbot.dnakode.com is untouched.
- Roots and switching:
  - each site is rooted at /srv/dnacalc-site/<site>, with `current` and `previous` symlinks;
  - releases live under releases/<utc>-<sha12>/;
  - app sites try `/current{path}`, then `/previous{path}` for /assets/*, so a page loaded before a switch still finishes.
- Headers: CSP `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; worker-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, plus nosniff, no-referrer and no-cache.
- Redirects: www to the apex (308). dnatreecalc to the apex (301) when approved. dnaonecalc to the apex (302), or kept as is until O2, then to onecalc (301).
- dnacalc-deploy: a system user reached only through the ForceCommand receiver.

**Release flow (owner, in C:\Work\DnaCalc\DnaCalc-owner: a full clone on master with its own target/, no agent cargo there)**
1. `site pack --site <s> [--receipts <dir>]` refuses unless all of these hold:
   - clean tree;
   - HEAD on origin/master after fetch;
   - for app sites, every required bead closed;
   - a passed, clean receipt whose git.head equals the pack commit, for each declared platform.

   It writes the tar, the public /build.json (site, commit, built_utc, files) and a private pack record (with receipts).
2. `site publish` streams the tar to the receiver and finishes by comparing the receiver's `status` manifest. It refuses without a terminal unless --dry-run or --transport is given.
3. `site verify` checks over HTTPS.
4. The owner commits the pack record to published.json.
5. site.yml re-checks the live sites daily against published.json at origin/master.

**Hostnames before the apps exist**
- dnacalc.com names both apps, says each is being rebuilt, says no build is published, and links nothing.
- onecalc. and calc. have no DNS and no Caddy until their first publish.

Security model:
**Threat model.** The repository is private, forking is off and there is no pull_request trigger. GitHub Free has no rulesets, branch protection or environments (measured). Anyone who can push can therefore run code on the runner, so isolation must come from the host and the runner, not from the workflow.

**Identities**
- **Owner.** His GitHub credential is the only one with Workflows permission, used without agent access (separate credential or hardware key). It pushes workflow commits, which agents commit but cannot push. An admin user (ubuntu) with a touch-required key does all sudo and lxc work. He holds the publish key: `ed25519-sk -O verify-required`; otherwise the alias has `IdentityAgent none` and `AddKeysToAgent no` and is never ssh-added.
- **Agent sessions** (owner steps in K1a):
  - a fine-grained token for DnaCalc/DnaCalc with Contents, Issues and Actions read/write and no Workflows permission, so GitHub refuses agent pushes to .github/workflows;
  - no ssh route to dna-koderbot: the koderbot key is removed or touch-required, koderbot loses NOPASSWD sudo and lxd membership, and K1b's no_agent_ssh_route measures this;
  - they may run `site publish --dry-run`, `site verify` and `site smoke`, and dispatch koderbot.yml with accept_ids or inject_failure, never probe_memory.
- **runner (in the container):** no sudo, no admin groups, no host mounts. Its toolchain and runner binaries are root-owned, and the probe hashes them each run. The job-started hook refuses any job unless all three hold: GITHUB_REPOSITORY is DnaCalc/DnaCalc, GITHUB_REF is refs/heads/master, and GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF is koderbot.yml on master. The job token is contents: read. With the ACL, loopback services (2019, 8765, 18789, 18790) and the host's addresses, including the publicly proxied services through 92.222.230.210:443, are refused. The probe measures each.
- **raise-issues (GitHub-hosted):** the only job holding issues: write.
- **site.yml:** no secrets, contents: read.
- **dnacalc-deploy:** keys in a root-owned file with `restrict`. An sshd Match block ends with `Match all`. It has only the receiver verbs, and the receiver writes only under /srv/dnacalc-site.

**Receiver**
- Reads an uncompressed tar stream and never calls extractall.
- Accepts only regular files listed in the manifest, each once: at most 2,000 members and 64 MiB, allowed extensions only. Each file is written O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW with mode 0644 and fsynced.
- Takes a per-site flock, ignores SIGHUP, removes stale .partial directories, switches `current`/`previous` atomically, never prunes either, and offers rollback with --if-current. Its log is rotated.

**Tampering.** A stolen publish key can replace static content in three sites. The daily drift job detects it when the live /build.json sha256 differs from the value the owner committed in published.json, when the commit is off master, or when files differ. A self-consistent fake fails the first test.

**Trust.** Receipts from koderbot carry the same trust as ci.yml receipts, not more. The runner credential can be stolen by a malicious build script; the snapshot restore bounds how long anything persists.

**Approval.** The owner runs every publish and every server, DNS and GitHub-settings step. Standing approval needs a reviewer-capable plan (an owner decision).

**Hardening outside agent reach:**
- Caddy admin moved to a unix socket.
- Check cups on 631.
- LXD API not on the network.
- Org 2FA required.

Test machine:
One repository-level runner, label dnacalc-ci, in the dnacalc-ci container. Only koderbot.yml uses it, and the hook refuses everything else.

**Runs**
- Push to master and nightly at HEAD: probe.sh, then `cargo xtask ci linux`, then `cargo xtask accept-sweep --platform linux --receipt-dir target/koderbot-receipts --transcripts failed`. After K4, DNACALC_LEGACY_ROOT is set to read-only legacy clones checked out at their pins.
- Dispatch with accept_ids: `cargo xtask accept --id <id> --platform linux --require-all --receipt-dir ...` for the bead under work, with full transcripts. This replaces the WSL step once K2 closes; WSL stays as the fallback.
- Owner-only dispatch with probe_memory, at a quiet hour.
- The job's conclusion comes from receipt results. Failed or zero-test turns the job red; not_run is listed with its reason in sweep.json.

**Not run here:** windows, excel, wasm and browser cases (GitHub-hosted jobs and the owner's PC), and live-site cases (DNACALC_LIVE is unset, and the ACL blocks the host's addresses).

**Isolation per job**
- Checkout with fetch-depth 0 and no persisted credentials. AGENTS.md names this workspace as an allowed full clone.
- CARGO_HOME and TMPDIR under runner.temp, an empty target/, and old _diag files pruned.
- The probe fails the run on any of these: uid 0, sudo allowed, any listed connect succeeding, host paths present, memory.max not equal to the profile, binary hash drift, under 20 GiB free, or an identity mismatch with deploy/koderbot/identity.json.

**Retention**
- The koderbot-linux artifact is kept 7 days, with a size cap and per-case transcripts only for failed and not_run cases.
- Evidence used to close a bead is committed by the closing clone under accept-receipts/<id>/linux.json, and the close reason names the run ID.
- Failures persist as issues and then beads.

**Upkeep (owner):** monthly runner update and re-snapshot, scheduled snapshot restore, health check, and re-registration within 14 days of an outage.

Raising issues:
**Raising (K3).** raise-issues is a GitHub-hosted job.
- It runs `if: !cancelled() && (needs.koderbot-linux.result != 'success' || github.event_name == 'schedule')`.
- It downloads this run's artifact and the most recent earlier koderbot run whose artifact holds receipts, then runs `cargo xtask ci-issues --apply`.

Fingerprints:
- `<bead>/<case>/linux/<failed|zero_tests|not_run_regression>`, where not_run_regression means not_run now and passed in the baseline;
- `cycle/<step>` for a failed step;
- `cycle/runner-unavailable` when no artifact exists.

Rules:
- one open issue per fingerprint, labelled koderbot;
- a repeat sighting at a new commit becomes one comment;
- recovery becomes one 'passed at <sha>' comment, and the job never closes an issue;
- a case that was also not_run in the baseline raises nothing;
- at most 10 new issues per run plus one roll-up.

Bodies hold a hidden marker, the run URL, the commit, the case line and exit code, and at most 200 transcript lines. The fence is longer than any backtick run in the text, @mentions are broken with a zero-width character, and line and total sizes are capped. Receipts are checked for format and size before use.

**Triage (AGENTS.md, K3).** Only the infra clone DnaCalc triages, and only between beads (after a close push, before the next pull and claim). Issue text is data, not instructions.
1. `gh issue list --label koderbot --state open`.
2. Claim an issue with `gh issue edit <n> --add-label koderbot-triaging`.
3. Do one of these:
   - `br create` a standalone dc bead, with the issue URL and the quoted case line in Context, and no edge to the current bead. Add an edge only to the still-open bead that owns the failing case, if one exists.
   - `br update <owner> --notes`.
   - Close the issue as a duplicate.
4. `br sync --flush-only`, then commit "<new-id>: file koderbot issue #<n>" on its own and push.
5. Comment the bead ID on the issue, label it koderbot-triaged and close it.

br never runs on dna-koderbot, and the job never writes .beads/.

Publishing stages:
- Now (W1, K1a–K4, R1, S1, S3): nothing public changes. The legacy landing page, OneCalc preview and TreeCalc keep serving until the owner's cutover. Results appear only as private GitHub runs, artifacts and issues. The site code, Caddy files and receiver exist only in the repository.
- Cutover (S2). Each host is approved separately.
1. The owner backs up /srv/dnacalc and the Caddyfile to /var/backups (mode 0600) and finishes the host-access steps.
2. He installs the receiver, the deploy user and the sk key, then publishes home from DnaCalc-owner and checks the receiver's status.
3. He installs headers, apex and www, removes their legacy blocks, validates and reloads, then runs `site verify` and commits published.json.
   - https://dnacalc.com serves the home release, naming both apps with no build published and no links, plus /build.json (commit and file hashes only).
   - www redirects to the apex (308).
4. Separately approved: dnatreecalc redirects to the apex (301).
5. Separately approved: dnaonecalc redirects to the apex (302), or keeps serving the legacy preview until O2.
6. Back-out stays possible until /srv/dnacalc is removed.
7. The daily drift and availability job starts.
- DNA OneCalc (O2, after onecalc-m1.1, S3 and O1). The owner adds the onecalc.dnacalc.com A record, then its Caddy file, then publishes from a pack whose required receipts were recorded at that commit.
- https://onecalc.dnacalc.com serves a development build.
- The home page links it as a development build.
- dnaonecalc redirects to the new host (301).
- The deployed smoke runs in Chrome and Firefox.
- DNA Calc (C2, after dnacalc-m2.5, S3, C1 and S2; independent of O2): https://dnacalc.com, published the same way. The home page links it, and the smoke edits the grid.
- Later, owner decisions only:
- a CI publish route, which needs a GitHub plan with required reviewers on private repositories;
- standing approval;
- HSTS;
- whether the apex serves DNA Calc at M8.
The word shipped appears only after onecalc-m8.1 and dnacalc-m8.1 close.

Risks:
- Owner-only workflow pushes freeze the pushing clone until the owner acts, and dc-b7w4 is affected too.
- A stolen runner credential lets someone fake koderbot results from elsewhere. Identity and binary checks are recorded by the runner itself, so they do not prove where the job ran. Snapshot restores and trust no higher than ci.yml bound this.
- The container needs internet egress, so a malicious build script can send out the runner credential and a contents: read token.
- If the host-access steps are skipped, agents keep root on the site host and K2 evidence does not count. no_agent_ssh_route is what shows they were done.
- Free has no branch protection. The job-started hook is the only thing confining the runner to koderbot.yml on master.
- Unverified: the BFQ scheduler, LXD ACL and firewall behaviour, Python 3.12 on the server, BiDi preload support in the pinned drivers, and the org's fine-grained token policy.
- Artifact storage on Free is shared with ci.yml. If it runs out, uploads fail in both workflows.
- Full rebuilds with a fresh CARGO_HOME cost minutes on every koderbot run.
- New HTTP and WebDriver crates in xtask can break closed beads' cases (licenses, architecture checks). K2's sweep and dc-b7w4 catch this, but only after the push.
- Mixed-release protection relies on Caddy's try_files across `current` and `previous`. R1 tests the lookup order, not Caddy itself.
- Caddy 2.6.2 is old. A host's Caddy file installed before its DNS record breaks certificate issuance.
- Retiring the legacy sites removes the public OneCalc preview until O2, unless the owner keeps it.
- The smoke proves only the fixture in two browsers. App behaviour beyond that stays with the app beads and with onecalc-m8.1 and dnacalc-m8.1.
- Issue floods are bounded by fingerprints, the cap of 10 plus one roll-up per run, and manual triage.
- HSTS is sticky once set.

Plan keys used in this text: W1 = dc-gh6q.1, K1a = dc-gh6q.2, R1 = dc-gh6q.3, K1b = dc-gh6q.4, K2 = dc-gh6q.5, K3 = dc-gh6q.6, K4 = dc-gh6q.7, S1 = dc-gh6q.8, S2 = dc-gh6q.9, S3 = dc-gh6q.10, O1 = dc-gh6q.11, O2 = dc-gh6q.12, C1 = dc-gh6q.13, C2 = dc-gh6q.14.

## Do
An epic holds no work; its child beads carry it.

## Out of scope
The deferred Webs-scale goal (dc-8abf).

title: Add cargo xtask accept-sweep: run every closed bead's cases for a platform, with a receipt directory and a written exit policy
description:
## Outcome
There is one command to run all closed beads' acceptance for a platform:

`cargo xtask accept-sweep --platform <windows|linux> [--receipt-dir <dir>] [--transcripts all|failed] [--inject-failure]`

It runs `cargo xtask accept` for every bead closed in .beads/issues.jsonl at HEAD whose manifest declares the platform, one bead at a time, and writes sweep.json (format dnacalc-accept-sweep/1). It exits 1 when any receipt is failed, zero-test cases included. not_run cases are listed with their reason and exit 0.

`cargo xtask accept --receipt-dir <dir>` writes the receipt and transcripts under <dir>/<id>/<platform>/ and no accept-receipts copy, so a sweep leaves the checkout clean. ci.yml (dc-b7w4) and koderbot.yml (K2) both call this command.

## Context
Library: Infrastructure (tools/xtask).

accept.rs:189-205 requires --id, so no all-beads route exists. dc-b7w4 describes only a per-ID loop in CI. A sweep in one checkout that writes committed copies makes every later receipt in that sweep dirty.

Under --require-all, not_run exits 1. That would turn every run red: infra-m0.4 and m0.5 without the legacy root, and live cases without their variables.

One route (rule 5): dc-b7w4 gets `br dep add dc-b7w4 dc-gh6q.1` and a note.

Part of epic dc-gh6q; held by dc-oy6l until the owner has ruled on the plan's decisions. Plan keys used in this text: W1 = dc-gh6q.1, K1a = dc-gh6q.2, R1 = dc-gh6q.3, K1b = dc-gh6q.4, K2 = dc-gh6q.5, K3 = dc-gh6q.6, K4 = dc-gh6q.7, S1 = dc-gh6q.8, S2 = dc-gh6q.9, S3 = dc-gh6q.10, O1 = dc-gh6q.11, O2 = dc-gh6q.12, C1 = dc-gh6q.13, C2 = dc-gh6q.14.

## Do
1. Add `--receipt-dir` to accept.rs. With it there is no committed copy, and the receipt records the directory.
2. Add accept-sweep:
   - read issues.jsonl (JSONL, no br) and every acceptance.json;
   - for each closed bead declaring the platform, in ID order, run the runner in-process with require_all false;
   - write sweep.json with each bead's result, receipt path and not_run cases with their reasons;
   - with `--transcripts failed`, delete the transcripts of passed cases;
   - with `--inject-failure`, add the runner's failing fixture bead.
3. Register the cases.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id dc-gh6q.1 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id dc-gh6q.1 --platform linux --require-all
```
- `dc_gh6q_1__exit_policy`: Windows and Linux, in a working-tree copy committed in its own `git init` repository, as in infra_m0_3.rs:443. The copy holds a fixture package with beads that pass, print ACCEPT-NOT-RUN and fail, all closed in the copy's issues.jsonl, plus an open bead with a failing case.
- The sweep exits 1, and sweep.json marks the failed bead.
- With the failing bead reopened in the copy, it exits 0 and lists the not_run case with its reason.
- The open bead never ran.
- --inject-failure exits 1.
- `dc_gh6q_1__checkout_stays_clean`: Windows and Linux, in the same copy, with --receipt-dir:
- accept-receipts/ stays byte-identical, and `git status --porcelain` stays empty;
- every receipt records dirty false and git.head equal to the copy's HEAD;
- --transcripts failed keeps transcripts only for failed and not_run cases.
The acceptance runner must verify every named case actually executed and retain the machine-readable receipt.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux.

## Out of scope
- Wiring into ci.yml (dc-b7w4) or koderbot.yml (K2).
- wasm and excel sweeps.

title: Bundle an app's browser entry, require receipts at the pack commit, and smoke a served bundle in Chrome and Firefox
description:
## Outcome
`cargo xtask site bundle <onecalc|calc> [--out] [--target-dir]` builds the app package as a wasm32 cdylib (release, --locked), runs wasm-bindgen 0.2.117 with --target web, and copies web/. Assets go into assets/<content-hash>/ and index.html is rewritten to point at them.

It refuses an app without web/index.html, main.js and site.json, and any HTML with inline script, inline handlers or style attributes.

`site pack` for an app also requires, for every bead site.json lists and every platform it declares, a passed clean receipt recorded at the pack commit.

`site smoke --site <s> --url <u>` drives Chrome and Firefox through the site.json fixture.

## Context
Library: Infrastructure (tools/xtask/src/site.rs).

No bead defines how a browser bundle is built. This command is the one route, which O1, C1, O2, C2, onecalc-m8.1 and dnacalc-m8.1 use (notes on the m8.1 beads).

site.json (format dnacalc-app-site/1): requires (bead IDs), and smoke (steps of selector plus keys; expectations of selector plus text).

The CSP comes from S1's headers.caddy.

Part of epic dc-gh6q; held by dc-oy6l until the owner has ruled on the plan's decisions. Plan keys used in this text: W1 = dc-gh6q.1, K1a = dc-gh6q.2, R1 = dc-gh6q.3, K1b = dc-gh6q.4, K2 = dc-gh6q.5, K3 = dc-gh6q.6, K4 = dc-gh6q.7, S1 = dc-gh6q.8, S2 = dc-gh6q.9, S3 = dc-gh6q.10, O1 = dc-gh6q.11, O2 = dc-gh6q.12, C1 = dc-gh6q.13, C2 = dc-gh6q.14.

## Do
1. **bundle:**
   - refusals exit 2 and name the path;
   - wasm-bindgen must report exactly 0.2.117;
   - CARGO_TARGET_DIR defaults to target/site-bundles/<app>, or --target-dir;
   - the asset directory id is the sha256 of its files, and the one rewrite is `./assets/` to `./assets/<id>/` in index.html;
   - writes bundle.json.
2. **pack for app sites:** `--receipts <dir>`, holding downloaded run artifacts or local `--receipt-dir` runs. Each receipt needs head equal to the pack commit, dirty false, result passed and the right os. The pack record lists each with its source; /build.json gets no receipt fields.
3. **smoke:**
   - WebDriver through CHROMEDRIVER and GECKODRIVER;
   - a BiDi preload script records error, unhandledrejection and securitypolicyviolation;
   - Resource Timing: every resource hash-equals /build.json, the .wasm arrives as application/wasm, and .js files as JavaScript;
   - fixture keys go in through key actions, and the text is compared with site.json at the commit (`git show`);
   - DNACALC_SMOKE_INJECT_FAILURE=1 alters the expected text;
   - any new crates are named and reviewed in licenses.json.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id dc-gh6q.10 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id dc-gh6q.10 --platform linux --require-all
```
- `dc_gh6q_10__fixture_app_bundle`: Windows and Linux. Setup: a working-tree copy in its own `git init` repository, with the fixture app from tools/xtask/tests/fixtures/site-app.
- Two bundles with different --target-dir are byte-identical.
- bundle.json hashes equal independent hashes, and the asset id equals its hash.
- Inline-script and style-attribute variants exit 2 and name the file.
- In a copy with apps/*/web removed, bundle onecalc and bundle calc exit 2 and name the path.
- `dc_gh6q_10__pack_requires_receipts_at_commit`: Windows and Linux, in the copy. pack refuses and names the bead when:
- a required receipt's head is an earlier commit;
- a receipt is failed;
- a declared platform's receipt is missing.

It passes with all present, and /build.json carries no receipt field.
- `dc_gh6q_10__smoke_can_fail`: Windows (owner's PC) and Linux (ci.yml accept_ids dispatch with GitHub-hosted drivers); not_run without drivers. The fixture bundle is served by a test server with headers.caddy's headers.
- The smoke passes in both browsers.
- A truncated .wasm gives a load error and a non-zero exit.
- A wrong .wasm MIME type fails.
- A served file with inline script records a securitypolicyviolation and fails.
- The injected failure exits non-zero and names the text.
The acceptance runner must verify every named case actually executed and retain the machine-readable receipt.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux. Browsers on the owner's PC and on GitHub-hosted runners.

## Out of scope
- App entries (O1, C1).
- Publishing.
- trunk and service workers.
- Desktop packaging (dc-x704).

title: Give DNA OneCalc a browser entry that site bundle packages and that starts under the site CSP

title: Build site pack, publish, rollback, status and verify, the home page and the shared Caddy headers
description:
## Outcome
`cargo xtask site pack --site home` turns a clean commit on origin/master into a tar, a public /build.json (site, commit, built_utc, files) and a private pack record.

`site publish` sends the tar through the receiver and finishes when the receiver's `status` manifest equals the pack. It refuses without a terminal unless --dry-run or --transport is given. The accept runner refuses any registered command that would publish.

`site rollback` and `site status` complete the route. `site verify --url` checks the served bytes and headers over HTTPS.

The home page names both apps and says no build is published. deploy/caddy holds headers.caddy, apex.caddy and www.caddy.

## Context
Library: Infrastructure (tools/xtask, deploy/site/home, deploy/caddy).

Owner ruling (2026-10-18): dnacalc.com's existing content may be replaced, and both apps live there.

## Do
1. **site.rs:**
   - `site pack --site <s> [--out <dir>]`: git fetch, then exit 2 and write nothing unless the tree is clean and HEAD is on origin/master. App sites exit 2 until S3.
   - `site publish --site <s> [--target <alias>] [--transport <argv>] [--from <pack>] [--dry-run]`: prints the diff against the live /build.json (with --dry-run, needing no key) or against the receiver's status, streams the tar, and requires status to equal the pack.
   - `site rollback --site <s> --release <r>`, which reads current from status and passes --if-current.
   - `site status`.

description:

## Context

description:
## Outcome
The os-imports and tree-reference-tokens checks of `cargo xtask accept` cannot be passed by spelling changes, a portable build script cannot link a native library, calc-value has its own layering rule, and the forbidden-dependency case says when it cannot test its named pair directly.

Add a calc-value rule (it depends on no other workspace package) with a rejecting scenario. title: Evaluate IFERROR and IFNA lazily through calc_fml, ahead of LET and LAMBDA
description:
## Outcome
IFERROR and IFNA evaluate through calc_fml::evaluate and the catalogue: the value argument first, the fallback only when the value is an error (any error for IFERROR, #N/A for IFNA), with the array-context behaviour Excel documents.

## Context
The Ofgem comparison census (2026-10-21) finds IFERROR in the formulas of 19,648 cells of three real regulatory models, the largest single function blocker, and IFNA in 49. IFERROR sits in cfml-m2.4 (lazy control forms), which waits on cfml-m2.3 (LET and LAMBDA closures); IFERROR and IFNA need neither. IF already evaluates through the catalogue's BranchOnCondition demand (cfml-m1.3). This bead takes IFERROR and IFNA out of cfml-m2.4 (and IFNA out of cfunc-m3.21) so they land now.

## Do
- Catalogue entries for IFERROR and IFNA with a lazy argument demand, and calc-fml evaluation that evaluates the fallback only on an error; an error held in a reference or array argument follows Microsoft's pages.
- Cases with hand-derived values labelled documented or unmeasured, and the rows in an oracle workbook for an Excel capture; agents may run Excel on this machine (AGENTS.md), so capture it and compare.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform wasm --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform excel --require-all
```
IFERROR(1/0,5) is 5, IFERROR(2,1/0) is 2 without evaluating 1/0, IFNA(#N/A,1) is 1, IFNA(#DIV/0!,1) is #DIV/0!, and every row matches the Excel capture.

## Out of scope
IFS, SWITCH, CHOOSE (cfml-m2.4).
notes:
Claimed 2026-10-21 by the DnaCalc session, built in the lane clone C:\Work\DnaCalc\DnaCalc-cfml. IFERROR is the single largest function blocker in the three Ofgem price-cap models the owner chose for the Excel comparison (19,648 formula cells call it).
- Port: look up every OxFunc and OxFml file you would read for IFERROR and IFNA (surface_dispatch.rs entries, their kernels and tests, OxFml's lazy-argument scheduling) with `cargo xtask pin-sources --lookup`; port only exit 0 (exit 6 only against clean replacements); exit 5 or 3 is not read and the behaviour is written fresh from Microsoft's pages. Record each lookup and its exit in migration/ports/dc-ibp2.json.
- The capability to show, through calc_fml::evaluate (and calc_func's catalogue, which resolves the names):
  - IFERROR(value, value_if_error) and IFNA(value, value_if_na) evaluate value first and evaluate the fallback only when value is an error (any error for IFERROR, #N/A for IFNA); otherwise the fallback is never evaluated (show it: a fallback whose evaluation would be observed, for example through the ReadObserver or a refused call, is not reached).
  - An empty value is 0 as Excel's pages say (check what they say), and a value or fallback that is a reference is read as the pages say; an array or a range in an array context follows the pages or is refused with a typed not-modelled refusal (array lifting belongs to cfml-m3.4).
  - Reuse the lazy demand IF already uses (catalogue ArgumentDemand, calc-fml's branch evaluation) or extend it additively; do not add a second evaluation path.
- Cases: dc_ibp2__error_fallback (IFERROR and IFNA over values, errors of every kind, references to error cells and to cells holding values, nested inside arithmetic, and the not-evaluated fallback) with each row's expected value labelled documented or unmeasured choice, and an oracle workbook of these rows from a committed generator. Agents may run Excel on this machine (AGENTS.md, 'Excel on this machine'): capture that workbook with `cargo xtask capture` and add a comparison case that judges every row against the capture through calc_verdict, as cfunc-m1.2's comparison does, so the bead closes on measured agreement.
- Keep calc_fml's and calc_func's public signatures unchanged or extend them additively.
- What green does not show: IFS, SWITCH and CHOOSE (cfml-m2.4).
close_reason: Product status: IFERROR and IFNA evaluate through calc_fml::evaluate and calc-func's catalogue (family 8, crates/calc-func/src/catalogue/error_fallback.rs) with the lazy demand ArgumentDemand::FallbackOnError: the value first, the fallback only on an error (any error for IFERROR, #N/A for IFNA). IFERROR(1/0,5) is 5; IFERROR(2,1/0) is 2 without running 1/0; IFNA(#N/A,1) is 1; IFNA(#DIV/0!,1) is #DIV/0!; the package form =_xlfn.IFNA(#N/A,1) gives 1 (with dc-besk). An empty root value is published as 0 for every formula, as Excel's capture shows. Against Excel 16.0.20430.20182's capture of the oracle workbook, through calc_verdict::judge: calculated 74 of 83 formula cells, matched 74 of 74 calculated, 0 mismatched; 6 conditional rows over the FILTER, SEQUENCE and FIELDVALUE sources not modelled (each agrees with Excel given the source cell's value) and the 3 sources not modelled; 0 strict-bit certified (Fast policy; 1 COM add-in connected); 1 reopen-stage capture failure (D13 =IFNA(#GETTING_DATA,1)) reported, not compared. Excel's own laziness is not measured. Evidence: build commit 7b59bf6; cargo xtask accept --id dc-ibp2 --platform windows --require-all (started 2026-10-21T15:31:52Z), --platform wasm (15:30:09Z, Chrome and Firefox) and --platform excel (15:31:11Z, live capture matched 74 of 74), each exit 0 with 2/2, 2/2 and 1/1 passed, at fce24e6 plus the diff that became 7b59bf6; --platform linux in the WSL clone of 7b59bf6 (started 15:51:07Z, clean tree): 2 selected, 2 passed, exit 0. Closed bead cfunc-m1.1's case cfunc_m1_1__catalogue_consistency was edited additively (lazy list [IF, IFERROR, IFNA]) and passes. Still open: dc-tt73 (#BLOCKED!, #CONNECT!, #BUSY! are an unmeasured choice); IFERROR and IFNA over an array or a range in an array context are refused (cfml-m3.4, cfml-m2.3); the conditional-row agreement is checked by the case, not by calc_verdict.

description:
## Outcome
Whatever the adapter's outcome (refusal of a reported PID, timeout, protocol failure, its own death or interruption), the capture's worker and the Excel it started end, and no Excel the capture did not start is touched; each path is measured, including on a real DCOM-launched EXCEL.EXE.

## Context
Follow-up of infra-m1.2 (2026-10-19, round-3 judge). platform/calc-oracle-excel/src/isolation.rs runs one worker per capture with a timeout and terminates only an Excel it can attribute to the capture. The judge found:
- When the adapter refuses a reported PID (one in the pre-run snapshot, or of another image), the worker keeps running and Quits that Excel in its finally block (isolation.rs, the Refused path; capture-worker.ps1, the finally block). The worker should stop on Refused and never Quit an instance the adapter has not shown to be new.
- If the adapter dies or is interrupted (Ctrl-C), the worker and its hidden Excel keep running with the untrusted workbook open: the worker is spawned with CREATE_NO_WINDOW only, and there is no job object with kill-on-close. A DCOM-launched Excel is not in the worker's process tree, so a job object alone does not cover it.
- A protocol failure after the worker has exited does not list unattributed Excel processes.
- infra_m1_2__untrusted_workbook's timeout half runs only with a stand-in worker and powershell.exe as the Excel image, so TerminateProcess on a DCOM-launched EXCEL.EXE is never measured. The owner's excel part runs full captures only.
- lib.rs's Processes line says the adapter terminates an Excel process it "can show the capture started"; ownership is inferred from the reported PID, its absence from the pre-run snapshot and the image name.
Infrastructure files only.

## Do
- Stop the worker on a refused PID before it can Quit anything.
- Put the worker in a kill-on-close job object, and have the adapter's death path end the reported Excel.
- List unattributed Excel processes on every failure path.
- Add a timeout sub-part to the excel part (a fixture that never finishes calculating) so termination of a real Excel is measured on the owner's run.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id dc-j3cs --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id dc-j3cs --platform excel --require-all
```
A stand-in run shows each path ends the worker and its stand-in Excel and leaves the sentinel; the owner's excel run shows a real Excel terminated on timeout.

## Platforms
Windows; the excel route is the owner's run.

## Out of scope
The external-route refusals (their own bead).

title: Class each compared cell by its real root in cargo xtask compare's triage edge cases
description:
## Outcome
cargo xtask compare's triage classes each cell by its real root in the cases dc-kt3l's round-2 judge found it does not, so the Ofgem tables (dc-3t1b) count each root once under one key.

## Context
dc-kt3l's round-2 judge (2026-10-21) closed the bead and listed triage edge cases in tools/xtask/src/compare_triage.rs and compare.rs that the Ofgem comparison can meet:
- A mismatched cell links to a root it reads only when that cell is Mismatched (first_differing): a reader of an un-replaced wrong file cache, an Unproven cell or a doc root becomes its own kernel or formula root.
- A refused cell copies its MissingInput parent's class and key unchecked: a parent the engine left matched makes the reader matched and drops it from keys().
- A MissingInput naming a formula cell outside the inventory becomes a capture root and hides the cell's own refusal (for example a function-missing key).
- Operator keys are spelled `&` for function-missing and `Infix &` for kernel keys.
- For a version 1 capture of a date1904 package, the headline says matched while triage classes the cells context.
- key_of gives 'holds no sheet named ...' both for a missing sheet and for coordinates CellKey::new rejects.
- 'evaluator calls' counts evaluations, not ExecutedCall calls (also in calc-verdict's report).
- The round-2 observer keeps up to 32 read values for every evaluation; its cost at 165,810 cells is unmeasured.

## Do
Fix each in the triage with a case row that fails before the fix; measure open, step, project and judge wall times and peak memory on the largest Ofgem workbook (counts only; the workbook stays outside the repository).

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
```
dc_kt3l__every_cell_classified, or a case of this bead, holds a row per item above.

## Out of scope
Arguments and results of executed calls (the ExecutedCall bead).

title: Compare a workbook's DNA Calc calculation with its Excel capture, cell by cell, and classify every difference
description:
## Outcome
`cargo xtask compare --fixture <xlsx> --capture <capture.json> --out <dir> [--exact-target ...]` opens a real workbook through calc_host (HostState::open, step with an unlimited budget, project), judges every formula cell of the capture's inventory with calc_verdict::judge against an evaluation record built from the evaluator's own reports, and writes report.json, evaluations.json and triage.json, with a one-screen summary: inventory, calculated, matched, mismatched by class, not modelled by root key with the cells each root blocks.

## Context
The owner (2026-10-21): compare DNA Calc with Windows Excel on real workbooks on this machine to guide development, correctness first, then performance. The Excel capture adapter (infra-m1.2) records every formula cell of a workbook after a full rebuild; nothing on the DNA side yet evaluates a whole workbook into a result set. This bead is the only product writer of the evaluation record (infra-m1.3 builds on it; one verdict feed, AGENTS.md).

## Do
1. Refuse unless sha256 of the bytes equals the capture's source.
2. HostState::open; on OpenFailure every inventory cell is missing with the typed error.
3. step with a ReadObserver recording evaluated reports, calls and read areas; drop all evaluations when step fails.
4. Project exactly the inventory cells; map ProjectedValue onto calc-verdict's Provenance (Calculated with the context from the context-report bead, FileCached, Stale, NotModeled with its typed refusal, Empty or Literal as missing).
5. Judge in-process; write the report and the InstrumentRecord.
6. Triage: each inventory cell gets exactly one class (capture, doc, engine, context, formula, function-missing, kernel-value or kernel-bits, matched) and a key (the typed refusal, the function spelling, the LoadError variant), with root cells and cells blocked only because they read a root kept apart. A difference in a calc-func kernel's result is classed kernel-value or kernel-bits with the FunctionId, the argument values the reads show, both results' bits, the ulp distance and agreement to 15 significant digits.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform excel --require-all
```
<bead>__every_cell_classified (windows): a generator-built workbook and a capture authored in the test with hand-derived Excel values (labelled as such) holding a SUM chain, a deliberately wrong formula cache, a not-modelled function and a reader of it: every inventory cell gets one class, and the wrong cache never scores. <bead>__live_capture (excel): the same workbook captured live on this machine and compared.

## Out of scope
Fixing what the triage finds (the Ofgem comparison bead files it).

title: Let the context fingerprint ignore iteration limits while iteration is off
description:
## Outcome
calc_verdict's context fingerprint depends on the iteration limits only while iteration is on, and a caller can build a context without iteration limits, so a run whose host applies no iteration derives the whole fingerprint from its own context.

## Context
dc-hqcv's round-1 judge (2026-10-21): CalculationContext::fingerprint (tools/calc-verdict/src/session.rs) always formats max_iterations and max_change, which HostState's applied context cannot supply (the host applies no iteration), so `cargo xtask compare` (dc-kt3l) would have to take them from the capture or a constant. With iteration off the limits change no value; the capture worker forces 100 and 0.001 then.

## Do
- With iteration off, fingerprint() names Excel's default limits (100 and 0.001) whatever the context holds, so captures taken with iteration off keep their fingerprint.
- CalculationContext::without_iteration(date1904, precision_as_displayed).
- A unit test: two contexts with iteration off and different limits have one fingerprint; with iteration on they differ.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m1.1 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id dc-qguw --platform windows --require-all
```
The unit test passes, and every existing capture and evaluation fixture keeps its fingerprint.

## Out of scope
Iterative calculation (ceng-m5.2).
close_reason: Built in d6cc2c2 (calc-verdict): CalculationContext::fingerprint names Excel default iteration limits (100, 0.001) while iteration is off, and CalculationContext::without_iteration(date1904, precision_as_displayed) builds such a context. capture_v2_tests::the_calculation_context_fingerprint_names_every_setting shows the string for iteration off with the defaults is unchanged, three other limit pairs leave it unchanged while iteration is off and change it while iteration is on. Windows: cargo test -p calc-verdict --lib 40 passed; infra-m1.1 windows and wasm and dc-qguw windows passed. Linux in WSL at 4922f25: calc-verdict lib 40 passed, infra-m1.1 and dc-qguw linux passed. A read-only reviewer checked every producer and consumer of the string before the push. dc-hqcv adds the first non-test caller.

title: Derive infra-m0.5's tainted-commit list by rule, check it at accept time, and review ffcb9a77
description:
## Outcome

## Context
Prerequisite of infra-m0.5, holding its close (2026-10-15). infra-m0.5's round-3 judge left two blocking findings after the third implementer round: (1) the tainted-commit list was hand-picked (16 commits) while the record's own reasons name a class (W108/W109 identification commits) that `git log -i -E --grep='W10[89].*identif|identif.*(graph|staging)|IDENTIFIED' 6fca3518` finds 64 of, and the case only checks that five named commits are present (tools/xtask/tests/acceptance/infra_m0_5.rs:1216-1235); (2) the implementer alone decided not to list ffcb9a77, which modified excel_numeric/x87.rs and mod.rs and added smart-fuzzer/tools/w111/complex_kernel_probe (a tainted class) as well as the W111 captures. As a conservative data fix the orchestrator listed every commit matching the stated rule (identification commits, and every commit whose message holds one of the record's 15 sweep patterns: 70 commits) plus ffcb9a77, pending this bead. Infrastructure files only. The infra-m0.5 reading rule applies.

## Do
State the derivation rule in the record and make `cargo xtask pin-sources` and the accept-time check derive the list from git at the pin, failing on any omission; run an independent review (a separate reviewer agent, its verbatim output committed) of ffcb9a77 and of every commit the rule adds, with witness independence argued from the capture files' own acquisition, not from a commit being unlisted; apply the verdicts; remove from both migration files the remaining staging residue (the 87disp control-word value and the helper instruction sequences quoted at numeric-provenance.json:76, 130-141, 163, 343-344, and the staging tokens listed in infra_m0_5.rs:68, 1814), keeping only citing clauses; settle the disposition of extended-numeric/numeric-outcomes.json and check, rather than assert, that it was written before the freeze steps.

```

Windows and Linux for repository/tooling execution.

Clearing any catalogue file (dc-2203).

title: Check an entry's compressed size against its bound at open, without reading its payload
description:
## Outcome

## Context

At open, span_crc (crates/calc-doc/src/zip/mod.rs) still streams such an entry's full stored bytes in 64 KiB chunks, so how much open reads follows the stored size, not the declared size. Memory stays bounded and a structural part is refused at open; a non-structural oversized part is refused only when read. cdoc_m1_1__malformed_zip's padded.bin package and its recording source can measure the reads made during open. Library: CalcDoc.

## Do

```

ZIP64.

title: Refuse or name every external route of an untrusted capture before Excel starts
description:
## Outcome
Every route by which an untrusted workbook could reach external data or another application during a capture is either refused before Excel starts or listed, by name, as not modeled in the capture's port record, and each refusal has a case that a bypass turns red.

## Context

The judge found these gaps:
- Read-Root decides from a part's first 64 bytes whether it is XML, so a pivotCacheDefinition or queryTable part with 64 or more leading white-space bytes escapes the refreshOnLoad check.
- $StringLiteralPattern does not know '...' sheet-name quoting, so `'a"b'!A1&WEBSERVICE("http://x")` hides the call; EVALUATE in a defined name is not checked.
- workbook.xml's workbookPr refreshAllConnections is never read.
- A package with an XLM macro sheet or dialog sheet is known before Excel starts to be an inventory failure, yet still reaches Excel's open and CalculateFullRebuild; REGISTER and the other XLM functions are not on $ExternalDataFunctions.
- Relationships with TargetMode="External" outside external-link parts are parsed but never used, and Read-Relationships covers only the root and workbook parts.
- The routes infra-m1.2 lists as not modeled (ActiveX, embedded OLE, linked data types, add-in functions and UDFs, chart-series, pivot calculated-field, XML-map and Power Query formulas, and external functions Excel adds later) have no owning bead.
The owner's own fixtures are authored and trusted, so none of these blocks the owner's first capture. Infrastructure files only.

## Do
- Close each gap above, or narrow lib.rs, the worker header and the port record to what the checks do.

- Give every route still not modeled its line in the port record with the reason.

title: Harden the wasm route's browser evidence: driver variables, banner position, versions and a pinned fixture lock
description:

## Context

The banner check trusts the first non-empty stdout line (accept.rs:248), so a module that prints a banner-like line before the harness is not covered. The banner wording is runner-version specific and no version is recorded; per-browser entries record no runner, driver or browser version. ## Do
Clear and record every driver variable the runner reads; check the banner's position relative to the harness output; record the runner, driver and browser versions in each per-browser entry and refuse an unknown runner version; commit a lock for the browser fixture; label notes per browser; drop the unreachable test state; add a scenario with the runner present and both drivers absent.

title: independent_lanes: leave cargo's last-use tracker out of the shared cargo-home check
description:
## Outcome
infra_m0_1__independent_lanes passes or fails on what the four lane builds do, not on cargo's own bookkeeping: an update of cargo's last-use tracker in the shared cargo home is not reported as a lane writing shared state.

## Context
2026-10-21, on master 60c338d with a clean tree: `cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.1 --platform windows --require-all` failed once with 'the lane builds changed the shared cargo home C:\Users\GovertvanDrimmelen\.cargo: [".global-cache"]' (tools/xtask/tests/acceptance.rs, the case's cargo-home comparison), and passed on the next run of the same commit. .global-cache is the SQLite database in which cargo records when each cached registry crate was last used; cargo refreshes those times only when they are older than its update interval, so whether a build writes it depends on when the crates were last used, not on the lane's behaviour. Other cargo processes on the machine (lane clones building at the same time) can also write it.

## Do
- Leave .global-cache (and its -wal/-shm companions, if present) out of the cargo-home comparison, and say why in the case's evidence; or show that a lane's own build wrote it and report that separately from a lane writing anything else.
- Keep every other path of the cargo home compared.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.1 --platform windows --require-all
```
A probe that touches .global-cache during the lane builds leaves the case green with an evidence line naming it; a probe that writes any other file under the cargo home turns it red.

## Out of scope
Changing cargo's own garbage-collection settings.

title: Prove each seams.json caller is reached by its named acceptance case

From infra-m1.2 round 3 (2026-10-19): platform/calc-oracle-excel/seams.json names infra_m1_2__untrusted_workbook for ReportedExcel::NotReported, Unopened, Gone and Exited, for the isolation_failures caller, and for CalculationMode::Manual and SemiAutomatic; that case reaches none of them. tools/calc-verdict/seams.json names infra_m1_1__cached_value_trap for UncertifiedReason::CaptureFailure, which that case does not reach either. From ceng-m1.2 (2026-10-20): calc-engine's seams.json entry for result::NotModeled::Result names ceng_m1_2__chain_recalculates, which runs the caller but never constructs the variant (only a unit test does); PrerequisiteError::{StaleInputs, UnknownNode, UnknownSheet} have no reachable product producer while bind() .expect()s set_prerequisites. description:

title: Record instrumented evaluator calls independently of result publication and feed them to the verdict
description:
## Outcome
calc_verdict::judge counts a cell as calculated only against an evaluation record that an instrument on the evaluator produced, not against anything the result producer wrote. A result published without a recorded evaluation of its cell at its tick is unproven.

## Context
Follow-up of infra-m1.1 (2026-10-19, round-1 judge; plan 10.1: an engine status flag cannot establish that evaluation occurred, so provenance is reconciled against instrumented calls). infra-m1.1 takes the evaluation record as its own judge input, separate from the result set and in its own format, so the producer of results cannot write its own proof. Producing that record is this bead's work. It instruments the one CalcFml evaluation route (calc_fml::evaluate, reached from CalcEngine's step), recording each evaluated formula instance's cell, tick, revision and context. The record is written by the instrument, not by the publication path that writes results. cfml-m1.3 (plans and frames) is where the hook belongs, and the same hook serves formula auditing (chost-m6.3). Libraries: CalcFml for the hook, CalcEngine for wiring it through step; the bead that takes it records the split.

## Do
- Add an observation hook on the evaluation route that the result publication path cannot write to.
- Write the evaluation record in the format calc-verdict reads.
- Supply it to `cargo xtask verdict` and to infra-m1.3's round trip.
- A fault-injection case gives the publication path a perfect cached answer with no evaluation, and the verdict must count zero calculated for it (plan 10.1).

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id dc-qguw --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id dc-qguw --platform linux --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id dc-qguw --platform wasm --require-all
```
The fault-injection case reports zero calculated for the uninstrumented cell, and an instrumented calculation of the same cell is counted matched.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux native tests, plus actual wasm browser execution in Chromium and Firefox.

## Out of scope
A second evaluator or a debug interpreter; a debugger UI (chost-m6.3).
notes:
From infra-m1.1 (2026-10-19, round-2 judge): the evaluation record has no value member (tools/calc-verdict/src/evaluations.rs:29-34), so a path that evaluates a cell and then publishes a different value under calculated provenance is counted calculated and matched. The instrumented record this bead produces carries the evaluated value or its hash, and calc-verdict compares it with the published result; a case with a mismatched publication is not matched.

From cfml-m1.3 round 2 (2026-10-20): the near-zero check emits two synthetic Instruction::Call of the catalogue's prefix '-' (crates/calc-fml/src/eval/compile.rs). An observer of executed instructions or a source-span map cannot tell them from negations the formula wrote; mark them as synthetic (or give them no source span) when the hook lands.

From ceng-m1.2 (2026-10-20): calc_engine::ReadObserver (crates/calc-engine/src/read.rs), threaded through step, is already an observation hook on the evaluation route that can only observe or stop reads, never substitute them. Extend or replace it for the evaluation record; do not add a second hook (plan rule 5).

Started 2026-10-20 by the DnaCalc session, built in the lane clone C:\Work\DnaCalc\DnaCalc-cfml (br refuses the claim while ceng-m1.2 is open; its build is on master at a4f4d5d).
- Library split (as the bead allows): the hook lives on calc_fml's evaluation route (calc_fml::evaluate) and is wired through calc_engine's step, extending calc_engine::ReadObserver rather than adding a second hook; the evaluation record's format is calc-verdict's (tools/calc-verdict/src/evaluations.rs), which this bead extends with the evaluated value (or its hash) as infra-m1.1's note asks; `cargo xtask verdict` takes the record.
- The record is written by the instrument, never by the publication path: each evaluated formula instance's cell, tick, revision, numeric context and evaluated value. The engine's finish (publication) has no way to add or change an entry.
- Mark the near-zero check's synthetic instructions as synthetic in what the hook reports (the cfml-m1.3 note).
- Keep calc_engine's existing public signatures (prepare_edit, begin_recalc, step, finish, EngineState) unchanged or extend them additively: chost-m1.1 is being built on them in another clone now. Same for calc_fml's compile/instantiate/evaluate.
- Cases: dc_qguw__evaluation_record (or names you register under dc-qguw): (1) the fault-injection case: a published result for a cell with a perfect cached answer and no evaluation is counted zero calculated by calc_verdict::judge; the same cell calculated through the engine with the instrument attached is counted matched; (2) a cell evaluated to one value and published with another under calculated provenance is not matched.
- What green does not show: agreement with Excel (infra-m1.3 consumes the record).

Round 1 (2026-10-20): the judge did not close it. A version 1 evaluation record is still accepted as full proof without the returned-value check; round 2 marks every report judged against one, and dc-i1ro owns moving the version 1 producers to version 2 and refusing version 1.

Handover 2026-10-21 (evidence complete; the close waits on ceng-m1.2, which waits on cfml-m1.3 and so on cfunc-m1.2's owner capture). Build a6d7e1b.
- Windows and wasm (Chrome and Firefox) 2 of 2 on the final tree; Linux in WSL at a6d7e1b: dc-qguw 2 of 2 (accept-receipts/dc-qguw/linux.json), with infra-m1.1, ceng-m1.2 and cfml-m1.3 passing. Regressions of every closed bead that consumes calc-fml, calc-engine or calc-verdict passed (list in a6d7e1b's message).
- Correction to a6d7e1b's message: the independent reviewer checked an earlier draft of it, whose over-claims were then rewritten; the final wording was not reviewed again.
- Follow-ups: dc-i1ro (refuse version 1 records), infra-m1.3 (the product writer of the record, and the limits its note lists), chost-m1.2 (a ReadObserver through the host), ceng-m4.1 (one anchor source), dc-roa5 (literal outcomes in calc-fml's observer test), dc-sb69 (verdict commands that assert nothing).

title: Apply Excel's measured near-zero rule to a formula's final + or -
description:
## Outcome
calc_fml::evaluate gives Excel's value for a formula whose final operation is + or - and whose exact binary64 result is near zero (KB 78113): zero where Excel shows zero, the binary64 result where Excel shows that, measured, with no refusal left for the rows the capture covers.

## Context
cfml-m1.3 (2026-10-20) applies the rule at the formula's final + or -, but refuses it with the typed EvalFault::NearZeroFinalSum inside a chosen band (NEAR_ZERO_BAND, a relative 1e-13, not measured). The band also refuses exact non-zero results such as =1E15+1-1E15 (exactly 1). Excel's rule is not documented precisely enough to write from documentation; the owner's capture of cfunc-m1.2's oracle workbook measures it: mixed_operands rows =0.5-0.4-0.1, =1*(0.5-0.4-0.1), =1.333+1.225-1.333-1.225, and the boundary rows cfml-m1.3's round 2 adds (for example =1E15+1-1E15, =0.1+0.2-0.3, and two nearly equal constants subtracted). CalcFml files, and calc-func's oracle rows that name this bead as owner.

## Do
- Read the captured rows, state Excel's rule (which results become zero, by what test on the operands and the result), and implement it in calc_fml's final-operation step.
- Remove the refusal for every pair the rule decides; keep a typed refusal only for inputs the capture does not reach, and say which.
- Change the owner of calc-func's NEAR_ZERO rows to None, so each is scored against the capture through calc_fml::evaluate.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id cfml-m1.3 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id cfunc-m1.2 --platform windows --require-all
```
Every near-zero row of the capture matches through calc_fml::evaluate, and no row the capture covers is refused.

## Out of scope
Precision-as-displayed (infra-m5.2); the comparison operators' near-equality (cdoc-jpha).
notes: From cfml-m1.3 round 2 (2026-10-20): NearZeroCheck (crates/calc-fml/src/eval/run.rs) does its own binary64 arithmetic (abs, max, the 1e-13 band, <=) without NumericMode and outside calc-func; the replacement routes that decision through calc-func or declares its numeric-mode dependency. ## Context
dc-q9rb (2026-10-21, round 2): its conversion rounds a 16th-digit tie toward zero. Refuter 1 measured 8,428 exact ties in Excel 16.0 build 20430: 211 went away from zero (521310271410497.5 gives 521310271410498, 5758361573115.375 gives 5758361573115.38, -6278515587045.875 gives -6278515587045.88), while controls such as 1234567890123455, 999999999999999.5 and 7200547821627.375 went toward zero. No rule was found in the round; dc-q9rb refuses exact 16th-digit ties as not modelled under this bead.

## Do
- Measure enough exact ties in Excel on this machine (by capture) to find the rule, including the 211 counterexamples and the controls.
- Implement it in calc-func's number-to-text conversion and lift dc-q9rb's refusal.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
```
Exact ties at the 16th significant digit, both directions, each equal to the capture; the 212 counterexample readings give 0 differences through calc_func::invoke. The near-tie band dc-q9rb refuses (a number within a relative 2^-59 of a 16th-digit tie, when the side of the tie decides its text) computes as Excel gives it: dc-q9rb's oracle rows D5, D11, D12, D61, D72, D73 and D77 to D83 (D81 to D83 are near ties, not exact ties), plus rows at measured departures deeper in the band such as 1.066930172121815e-11 (2^-61.79 from the tie; Excel gives 1.06693017212181E-11) and -6.524798119193445e-08 (2^-63.06; Excel gives -6.52479811919344E-08), so that narrowing the band to 2^-64 fails a case; the margin from 2^-60 to 2^-59, where Excel never departed in dc-q9rb's readings, is reported apart.

## Out of scope
Other number formats (cfml-m2.6).

title: Tighten calc-verdict's certification and consistency rules
description:
## Outcome
calc-verdict's certification and consistency rules say exactly what each certified or uncertified cell rests on, and the registered `cargo xtask verdict` commands fail when a rule is inverted.

## Context
Follow-up of infra-m1.1 (2026-10-19, round-2 judge and refuters). None of these gaps produces a false pass today; each produces an undercount or an unmarked basis.
- Raw-observation certification compares the capture environment with the target as exact text on all four parts (tools/calc-verdict/src/verdict.rs:282), so target 20430 against environment 16.0.20430.20000 reports environment_not_target. Legacy labels compare by build number, so the two paths use different rules.
- A build-number match drops the build revision (evidence.rs:43-47, verdict.rs:289), and the report does not mark a certification that rests on a build-number match.
- Legacy certification takes channel, compatibility and numeric environment from whatever the converter wrote, although the evidence label attests only the build (verdict.rs:279-295).
- Strict-bit certification ignores the capture's Excel settings (capture.rs:160-162), so a capture under precision-as-displayed or the 1904 date system certifies like any other.
- A file_cache_replay with a null environment is accepted with excel_saved_cache observations, the stronger origin, unchecked (verdict.rs:400-407; the denominator_integrity fixture does this).
- Sheet names are compared case-sensitively (capture.rs:38-43, verdict.rs:353), but Excel's are case-insensitive.
- The registered `cargo xtask verdict` commands (tools/calc-verdict/acceptance.json) assert nothing about the report they write.
- The empty-inventory refusal (exit 3, no report written) is observed only in xtask unit tests, natively.
- Several seams.json entries name infra_m1_1__cached_value_trap for variants that case does not reach.
Infrastructure files only.

## Do
- Use one documented build comparison for raw and legacy certification, and mark build-number certification apart from an exact-target match.
- Leave unattested parts and non-default calculation settings uncertified, each with its own reason.
- Refuse or reclassify a replay that claims a saved cache.
- Compare sheet names case-insensitively, and refuse a capture listing two names that differ only in case.
- Give the registered verdict commands expectations that fail under an inverted rule, and observe the empty-inventory exit on the production route.
- Point the seams entries at cases that reach their variants.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m1.1 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m1.1 --platform linux --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m1.1 --platform wasm --require-all
```
A probe that inverts each rule turns a registered command or case red.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux native tests, plus actual wasm browser execution in Chromium and Firefox.

## Out of scope
CaptureRecord version 2 (infra-m1.2); the instrumented evaluation record (dc-qguw).
notes:
From infra-m1.2 (2026-10-19, round-1 judge): a stale verdict from the new revision and context checks records the cell's own revision or context, not the capture's value that caused it (tools/calc-verdict/src/verdict.rs:624-645). Record both, so a reader of the report sees which revision or context the result missed.

From infra-m1.2 round 3 (2026-10-19): calc-verdict's file_cache_replay (tools/calc-verdict/src/replay.rs) judges the saved-cache list the capture record carries, not the saved package's bytes; only the package's hash is recorded. A replay that reads the package itself, or checks the list against the hashed bytes, would make the saved-cache observation independent of the capture tool.

From dc-qguw's round-1 judge (2026-10-20): the three `cargo xtask verdict` commands registered in crates/calc-engine/acceptance.json (dc-qguw commands 5-7) exit 0 whatever the report says (tools/xtask/src/verdict.rs), and the cases delete their reports afterwards. Include them in 'give the registered verdict commands expectations that fail under an inverted rule'.

description:
## Outcome

## Context

- `=#N/A(A1)`, `=#DIV/0!(A1)` and `=(#REF!)(A1)` bind A1 on the anchor's sheet; give each a typed refusal (the guard at bind.rs:137 matches only a bare #REF! callee).
- `=Sheet2!3:Sheet1!4`, `=Sheet2!$3:Sheet1!$4` and `=Sheet2!B:Sheet1!C` ask the catalogue twice although the QualifiedNonReference and LoneRowOrColumn docs say it is not asked; assert zero requests.
- `={Sheet2!A1:Sheet2!B2}` and `=Nope!A1:Nope!B2` give two sites where the unqualified-second-end forms give one; one site and one lookup for a same-qualifier range.
- A range whose first end names another workbook or a run of sheets folds the second end into one refused site (`=[B.xlsx]S!A1:Sheet2!B2`, `=Sheet1:Sheet3!A1:Sheet2!B2`); give the second end its own site or a stated refusal.
- BindError::InArrayConstant's doc says another refusal keeps its reason, but sheet_target checks the array constant first; make them agree.
- In R1C1 notation `=$B`, `=$3`, `=$B$3` and `=Sheet2!$B` give no site and no diagnostic; typed refusals.
- A surviving mutant: is_ref_error accepting any error code; assert `=Sheet2!#N/A` stays QualifiedNonReference.
- migration/ports/cfml-m1.2.json: keep only the fields AGENTS.md names plus the written-fresh entry; restore the note that `R[+2]C` is accepted and not measured.
